rv.q: All of which is true with this impeccably cast and staged show.
It’s a thoughtful and moving play, receiving a lovely production at Writers Theatre filled with soulful performances.
It's a stunning production that should be seen at least once, though I, for one, wish I could see it a dozen times or more.
This is a thrilling night of theater in which an incredibly talented cast takes on some of life's biggest issues in lyrical fashion.
Writers Artistic Director Braden Abraham has deftly followed the brushstrokes of the master Mr. Friel in creating this entire world of contradiction and mystery.
This story of a go-between, caught between two ideologies or two TRANSLATIONS, so completely fascinating and realistic.

Tyler Meredith's Maire, set on emigrating to the United States, studies geography to help her figure out what her new land will be like (unless Manus can somehow figure out a way to make enough money to ask her to marry him). Sarah (Julia Rowley), who is apparently near-mute, struggles to just say her name.
Everything in this production supports the narrative being told.
It is the characters and their relationships that are the key to this story and worth the 2 hours and 20 minutes to wonderful storytelling.
